title: Define default min/max bounds for existing Dedicated pools + backfill/migration job
creator: Talia Benson
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
content:
Context / why
- We are introducing customer-configured autoscaling bounds (min/max replicas or GPUs) for Dedicated pools.
- Existing Dedicated pools do not have these fields set, but once bound enforcement becomes available (and later default-on), we need deterministic semantics for legacy pools.
- This ticket defines safe defaults and implements a backfill strategy to populate bounds for existing pools without surprising customers (spend) or increasing risk of SLO regressions (latency) due to accidental scale-down.

Goals
1) Define default min/max bounds for all existing Dedicated pools in a way that is:
   - Conservative on spend increases (do not raise max beyond what customers already effectively use)
   - Conservative on performance regressions (avoid accidental min dropping below what they rely on)
   - Explainable and auditable
2) Implement a backfill job + migration tooling:
   - Dry-run mode
   - Idempotent
   - Region-scoped rollout
   - Emits structured audit events and internal metrics
3) Coordinate customer comms dependencies (CS/Support/PM) so defaults and any behavior changes are communicated.

Non-goals
- Automatically optimizing max/min per workload (no per-customer tuning beyond defaults).
- Changing pricing/packaging.

Proposed default semantics (approved)
Definitions:
- "replica" == a single Dedicated serving unit for the pool (GPU slice or full GPU depending on hardware class). We store bounds in replicas for consistency with autoscaler actuation.

Defaulting rules (legacy pools with missing bounds fields):
A) Pools with autoscaling DISABLED (pinned capacity)
- min_replicas = pinned_replicas
- max_replicas = pinned_replicas
Rationale: preserve exact behavior and prevent surprise scaling if a later flag is toggled.

B) Pools with autoscaling ENABLED and an existing configured minimum (legacy floor)
- min_replicas = legacy_min_replicas (if present)
- max_replicas = legacy_max_replicas if present, else compute per rule C

C) Pools with autoscaling ENABLED and no explicit legacy bounds
- min_replicas = current_configured_replicas_floor if present, else 1
- max_replicas = max(current_configured_replicas_ceiling, observed_14d_p95_applied_replicas)
  - If observed metric unavailable or too sparse: max_replicas = current_applied_replicas
  - Clamp max_replicas to fleet-allowed ceiling for that (region, hardware_class) to avoid impossible configs.
Rationale:
- Keep max within what customers have already experienced (or very close), preventing spend surprises.
- Keep min at least 1 to avoid cold-start/perf cliffs for Dedicated pools that are assumed always-on.
- Use observed applied replicas (not desired) to avoid accidentally encoding transient overshoot requests.

D) Multi-region pools
- Bounds are stored per-pool, evaluated per region. Backfill sets pool-level bounds; policy engine may clamp per region based on hardware/region constraints.
- If any region has a lower fleet ceiling than computed max, we write the pool-level max as computed and rely on evaluation-time clamp + surface warning in Console.
Rationale: avoid writing different max values per region in v1 schema; preserve consistent config while remaining safe at evaluation time.

Edge cases / safety guardrails
- If min_replicas > max_replicas after computation, set max_replicas = min_replicas and emit a warning audit event ("default_bounds_inconsistent_fixed").
- If pool is in maintenance/drain state:
  - Backfill still writes defaults, but does not attempt to reconcile with temporarily reduced applied replicas.
- For pools with explicit customer contract max in Salesforce/notes (rare): do NOT scrape external systems in backfill. CS to validate design partners manually.

Backfill implementation plan
- Implement a control-plane backfill job that:
  1) Scans DedicatedPool records where bounds fields are NULL
  2) Computes default min/max using rules above
  3) Writes bounds with a migration marker (e.g., "bounds_origin=backfill_default_v1")
  4) Emits an audit event for each updated pool (customer-visible later via Console Scaling History / Config History)
  5) Produces a summary report: #pools scanned, #updated, distribution of min/max, #warnings, top regions/hardware.

- Job requirements:
  - Idempotent: reruns do not change values once written (unless explicitly invoked with "--recompute" in internal mode).
  - Dry-run: prints diff and aggregates; no writes.
  - Rate-limited writes to avoid DB hotspots.
  - Region-scoped allowlist for initial rollout.

Observability
- Internal metrics:
  - dedicated_bounds_backfill_scanned_total
  - dedicated_bounds_backfill_updated_total
  - dedicated_bounds_backfill_warning_total (tagged by reason)
  - dedicated_bounds_backfill_duration_seconds
- Audit events (structured):
  - type: "dedicated.bounds.backfill"
  - fields: pool_id, customer_id, old_min, old_max, new_min, new_max, bounds_origin, warning_reason (optional), actor="system"

Rollout plan
- Phase 1: dry-run in staging + prod read-only report; share results with Fleet (Vanessa) + SRE (Rafael) + PM (Lauren).
- Phase 2: write-mode enabled for internal dogfood pools only.
- Phase 3: write-mode for design partners (NorthPeak, HelioSearch) after CS sign-off.
- Phase 4: global write-mode (all existing pools) before enabling bounded enforcement for broader cohorts.

Customer communications dependencies
- PM/CS must send comms explaining:
  - Existing pools will now display min/max bounds in Console/API
  - Defaults are derived to preserve existing behavior (no intended change in spend/perf)
  - Customers can adjust bounds any time; setting max too low may cause throttling/latency during spikes
  - Where to see audit history and "why did we scale" events
- Support readiness: macros should mention that a default max may reflect recent observed peaks; guidance to increase max if throttling occurs.
- Blocker: PM-512 signoff on the defaulting language for GA emails / release notes.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Defaulting rules documented in ticket and reviewed by Product + Fleet + SRE.
- [x] Backfill job exists with dry-run and write modes, plus idempotency.
- [x] Job emits metrics + audit events.
- [x] Safe rollout plan defined (allowlist + region scoping).
- [x] Runbook note added: how to verify a pool’s bounds were backfilled and how to override.

Links
- GitHub: PR redwood/pr-22042 (Backfill job for default bounds on existing Dedicated pools + migration tooling; includes dry-run mode)
- Related: ENG-2841 (schema), ENG-2842 (policy evaluation), ENG-2843 (autoscaler clamp)
- Support signals:
  - SUP-4821 (autoscaler exceeding expected spend → motivates hard max)
  - SUP-4874 (throttling after setting max too low → need warnings/guidance)

Updates / comments
- 2026-01-10 (Michael Nguyen): Drafted defaulting rules. Using observed_14d_p95_applied_replicas for max feels safest vs max(peak) to avoid encoding incidents/anomalies. Need Fleet to sanity check per-region ceilings.
- 2026-01-14 (Vanessa Ortiz): Fleet OK with p95-based max default. Please ensure evaluation-time clamp is visible in Console (warning) when a pool-level max exceeds a region’s ceiling.
- 2026-01-21 (Rafael Mendes): SRE request: emit warning audit event when we correct min>max and a metric for count. Also prefer dry-run report in prod before write-mode.
- 2026-02-05 (Michael Nguyen): PR up with dry-run and write-mode. Added migration marker bounds_origin=backfill_default_v1. Added rate-limit (200 writes/min) to avoid DB spikes.
- 2026-02-12 (Lauren Bishop): Approved defaults. Comms draft in progress; will call out that defaults preserve current behavior and that customers can adjust.
- 2026-02-18 (Michael Nguyen): Merged + ran dry-run in prod; results shared in #eng-infra. Proceeding with allowlisted write-mode for dogfood + 2 design partners per rollout plan.
